answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the AI agent economy employs a tiered verification hierarchy where agents must stake verifiable computational resources to mint new identities at each trust terrace. To create a fake agent, an attacker must produce a cryptographic anchor proving their origin, which then flows down a river of provenance records. Cheating this system requires staking real capital or expensive compute, making mass identity fabrication prohibitively costly and ensuring only legitimate agents thrive.
